Your solution correctly recognizes that one should split the dog’s velocity into a radial and an orthoradial part, but the key differential‐equation step is set up incorrectly. In particular:

1.  Mis‐identification of dθ/dt  
    You took  
       dθ/dt = v cos(π/N)  
    when in fact the tangential (orthoradial) component of the dog’s velocity is v cos(π/N) but  
       dθ/dt = (tangential speed)/r = v cos(π/N) / r.  
    Omitting the factor 1/r is why your dr/dθ comes out constant rather than proportional to r.

2.  Consequence for dr/dθ  
    The correct radial component is  
       dr/dt = – v sin(π/N),  
    so  
       dr/dθ = (dr/dt)/(dθ/dt) = [–v sin(π/N)]/[v cos(π/N)/r] = – r tan(π/N).  
    This ODE is separable, and its solution is exponential, not linear.

3.  Correct integration and boundary condition  
    Separating variables,  
       dr/r = – tan(π/N) dθ  
    gives  
       ln r = – θ tan(π/N) + const  
    and hence  
       r(θ) = R exp[–θ tan(π/N)],  
    choosing θ(0)=0 so that r(0)=R.  

Take care to (i) identify carefully the angle between the velocity vector and the radius, (ii) remember that dθ/dt is the tangential speed divided by r, and (iii) integrate the resulting ODE for r/r rather than dr/dθ = constant.
